items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: I think Simon or somebody wrote me up in one of the New York newspapers as being the house drummer of Broadway.

ctx.x: Well, he was up there to see Frank all the time and his old friend whom he loved, was Tommy Dorsey. So we opened that show that summer -- the summer replacement show, which was on Saturday nights. While we were at these four weeks at the Paramount Theatre. In other words, we doubled, which was a hell of a job, because on Saturdays and Sundays -- and Fridays -- Frank was doing five shows a day, sometimes six, and we had to arrange the shows so that we could go over -- it was only four or five blocks up to the CBS…

We'd have cabs waiting for us, and we'd rush over there with no rehearsals, because we knew the music, and we'd do the show, our fifteen-minute segment. And we're still running back and forth with drums and so forth. I later on played that show with four different bands, after the Dorsey show band, I think Simon or somebody wrote me up in one of the New York newspapers as being the house drummer of Broadway.
Back to the Bandstand show, we did two weeks I'm sure of, and maybe three -- and we followed, we got there
